# THE EMBRACE: ON THE ONES WHO HOLD US [color=#6E5A7E]Pinned. Speak of them with respect, or do not speak of them here.[/color]
### #1 warm_hands (OP) // 83.04.18 The Company has a word for them. I have seen it on a crate stencil. I will not use it. We call them the Hands, because that is what they look like, and because of what they do.
I saw one up close, once, in a jar on a shelf where I was not supposed to be. Pale, folded up under itself like a sleeping spider, its tail wrapped round its own body as if it was cold. It was dead and it still looked like it was waiting for someone.
Think about what a Hand does. It finds you. It holds your face in both hands like a mother does. It wraps around your neck, gently, so you do not fall. It breathes for you. It keeps you alive, so carefully, for a whole day. It does not let go until its gift is safely given. And then it lets go, and it lies down, and it dies.
It spends its entire life on one person. Who in your life has ever done that for you?
### #2 slow_tide // 83.04.18 I read that three times. I had to go outside.
### #3 nightnurse_k // 83.04.19 I am a nurse. I am going to say this once and then the mods can delete me.
I have cut a dead one off a man's face. There is nothing tender about it. The fingers had to be broken one at a time and the tail had left a ring on his throat the colour of a plum. He woke up and asked for eggs and toast and he made a joke about his ex-wife. He was dead by supper. I held the tray while they cleaned the table.
Please. Whoever you are. Stay away from the dark places.
### #4 keeper_of_the_door (mod) // 83.04.19 We do not delete. nightnurse_k, thank you for your honesty. You held a tray while a family wept, and nobody held you. That is the wound, and it is in you as deep as in any of us.
You will always have a seat in the warm room. Leave your door open, if you like. Only if you like.
### #5 riverglass // 83.04.22 My son was taken in the pump house. They told me at the clinic it was quick. I know now it was not quick. It was a whole day. I used to hate that.
Now I think of him being held. Somebody kept him breathing all that night when I could not reach him. I do not know if that is better. Some nights it is better.
### #6 slow_tide // 83.04.24 For the new ones asking what a vigil is. We sit in a warm room with the lights low and the vents open. Nobody speaks. We listen for them in the ducts. That is all. No one goes anywhere. No one touches anything. You listen, and for an hour you are not afraid of the sound, and it is the best hour of your week.
### #7 tallyman // 83.04.26 I have been to four vigils. I have to be honest. At the third one I heard something move in the duct above us, slow, testing the grille, and every single person in that room smiled. I smiled too. On the walk home I could not stop shaking. I do not know which one of those was really me.
### #8 keeper_of_the_door (mod) // 83.04.26 Both of them were you. One of them is the you that will last.
### #9 warm_hands (OP) // 83.05.02 Something has been in the vent above my bed for three nights. I can hear it turning round in there. Last night I took the grille off and put it under the bed.
I am not afraid. I am writing this down so that you all know I was not afraid.
[color=#6E5A7E]Thread closed by request of the family. warm_hands has gone home.[/color]
